speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Education with regard to giving our ITE and polytechnic students more regional exposure under the Global Education Programme (a) whether there will be more funding resources to support overseas internship opportunities; (b) whether there is concrete and strategic support for regional interaction and exchanges in the cultural, arts and sports fields; and (c) how effective is the Opportunity Fund in supporting students from low-income families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The polytechnics and ITEs fund these programmes with support from the Ministry of Education (MOE) and other Government agencies, providing subsidies for airfare, accommodation and other out-of-pocket costs that students incur.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: It is also common for polytechnics and ITEs to tap on funds raised from donors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Singaporean students from lower-income households can also tap on the MOE Opportunity Fund for additional assistance and funding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: As for culture, sports and arts, students do participate in overseas arts performances, friendly matches and other sports competitions with their counterparts in the region.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The students typically take part in such activities as part of their co-curricular activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The level of funding support has been adequate to help our polytechnic and ITE students take up overseas exposure programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education)
text: If the Member is aware of any particular case that needs help, please let us know and we will certainly follow up with the students or the students may want to approach the management of the ITE or polytechnic.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, with regard to the Global Education Programme, the sub-component of it oversees industrial attachment programmes in the region.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share how many students so far have benefited from it as part of the total amount because it is also related to what the Minister for Trade and Industry mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The industrial attachment programmes help to train not just the workers but our future workers through the students.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned that funding resources are adequate at the moment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are there plans to enhance funding for the Global Education Programme for the ITEs and also the polytechnics, going forward?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This does not include the manpower and other costs of mounting the programme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Member is right, there is an Overseas Industrial Attachment Programme, there is also the Overseas Student Exchange Programme and Overseas Service and Development Programme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, the 4,000 students actually cover the three programmes.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In terms of funding, other than the Global Education Programme, I am happy to update Mr Saktiandi Supaat that there is also the Opportunity Fund that I briefly talked about.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Another interesting change is, previously when the institutes of higher learning were administering the disbursement of the Opportunity Fund, there is a gross monthly household income criterion of $4,000.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We want ITEs and also the polytechnics to have the flexibility to decide the subsidy level for the students and to tier the level of support based on the needs and also profile of the students.
